name: Герои Эхо недели дворфов — долинные ткачи, отбившие нашествие Хатун-Руми «Дорога вниз» (ADR-0023, ADR-0024; docs/content/герои/состав-героев.md, «Дворфы — Хатун-Руми»; RS.weeks в design/ui/roster.js). Пятеро по герою за цикл II–VI: c2-48 Тикку Режущий Мосты, c3-50 Маюк Плетёный Щит, c4-50 Ойка Травница Долины, c5-56 Хасси Пращница, c6-49 Руа Развязывающая Узлы. Задание 30.09.2026: портреты для окон призыва и Эхо вместо инициалов. Рецепт — принятый отряд Иш-Кантуна (jobs/heroes-echo-ishkantun.json): стиль, запреты, референсы стиля, кадр по пояс, корпус вправо, камера чуть снизу; способ «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md). Раса — Забытые, облик ни на кого из нынешних не похож. Долинные ткачи — решение агента по главам: лёгкие и жилистые, с длинными ловкими пальцами, глаза бледного золота, волосы цвета некрашеной шерсти даже у молодых — в тонких косичках с цветной пряжей; всё тканое: одежда, пращи, щиты, верёвочные мосты; полосы и ступенчатые узоры без знаков. Враги недели — каменщики, пращники и жрецы с узловыми шнурами Хатун-Руми (jobs/echo-hatunrumi.json) — только трофеи и угроза за правым краем. Класс — по оружию и действию, школа — по цвету света. Детали, которых нет в «кто он» и главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no gems or badges of rank. No inscriptions and no letter-like patterns on cloth or cords. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. The hero is not a dwarf: slight and light-boned, not short and broad, no long braided beard.

heroes.frame:
Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

The hero belongs to the valley weavers — a forgotten people who lived long before all the peoples of today, in a green mountain valley below the terraced mountains of Hatun-Rumi. Everything they own is woven: clothes, belts, slings, shields and the rope bridges over the gorges. They look unlike any people living now: slight, wiry and light-boned, with long, very nimble fingers; round faces with wide cheekbones, small chins and large, clear eyes of pale gold; their skin is a warm tawny brown; their hair is naturally the colour of undyed wool — cream, grey and pale fawn even in the young — and they wear it in many thin braids tied with bits of coloured yarn. They wear tunics and mantles of hand-woven wool in bold stripes and stepped bands of rust red, ochre, indigo and cream — patterns only, never signs; woven belts, bone needles, spindles, bronze knives and braided grass ropes. Their enemies were the stone lords of Hatun-Rumi — short, very stocky mountain dwarves with long beards braided and bound with knotted cords, who carried stone shields and woollen slings, wrote nothing and kept every debt in knots on long cords, and built walls of huge many-sided stones fitted without mortar; such things appear only as trophies or as the threat beyond the right edge.

jobs.title: Тикку Режущий Мосты — Забытые, контроль (на контроль), Воздух (c2-48, Эхо, уникальная)

jobs.subject: Subject: Tikku Bridge-Cutter, a man of the valley weavers, a controller of the Air school. Who he is: in the valley everyone weaves, and he wove the rope bridges himself — so he knew rope better than those who crossed it. When the masons of Hatun-Rumi came down into the valley over the rope bridges, barefoot and fast, with stones on their backs, he cut six bridges in one night, and the seventh at dawn, when the runners were already in the middle. Right now his knife is in the last rope of the seventh bridge. Character: quick, fearless and cold with anger — he hates the knot on the priests' cord that said the valley was already theirs; his teeth bared, his pale-gold eyes narrowed and fixed on the bridge beyond the right edge. Pose, the moment of the cut: the camera is low; he leans low over the anchor post of a rope bridge on the edge of a gorge, turned toward the right, his whole body driven into the stroke. He has exactly two arms: his far hand grips the thick braided grass rope where it is tied to the wooden anchor post; his near hand has just slashed a short bronze knife through it, and the cut rope springs apart in a burst of fibres. The bridge swings away toward the right over the abyss, and a gust of pale white-green wind of the Air school howls up out of the gorge, whipping the loose ropes and his braids. Details that tell his story: (1) the rope is his own weaving — thick braided grass, its fibres springing apart at the cut; (2) his fingers are calloused from the loom, a cut rope-end is tucked in his belt; (3) the handle of the bronze knife is wrapped in striped wool; (4) a hewn, square slinger's stone flies past his head from the right; (5) a coil of spare rope over his shoulder. Place: a deep gorge at dawn: the swaying rope bridge stretching away over the misty abyss, terraces of fitted grey stone and snowy peaks on the far side, a pale sky. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the depth of the gorge below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Mayuk Woven-Shield, a man of the valley weavers, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: his shield was woven by the whole valley — every house gave one strip with its own pattern — and a stone does not break a woven shield, it sinks into it like a foot into wet wool. He stood in the mouth of the valley behind it for nine days while the shield was mended behind his back, and he knew by the patterns whose hands were still alive. Right now the slingers of Hatun-Rumi loose a volley at him. Character: grim, enduring and full of hard anger — anger enough for two; his jaw clenched, his brows lowered, his pale-gold eyes burning over the rim of the shield. Pose, the moment of the volley: the camera is low; he stands square in the narrow mouth of the valley, turned toward the right, his weight sunk low into the blows. He has exactly two arms: his near arm holds up a huge round shield of thick woven wool and reed, braced toward the right, and hewn stones strike it and sink into its weave; his far hand grips a heavy wooden club edged with bronze, held low behind the shield. Amber-orange light of the Earth school bursts from the stony ground at his feet, grit and wool fibres fly. Details that tell his story: (1) the shield is made of many strips in different stripes and stepped bands, each strip from a different house; (2) several square hewn sling-stones are stuck in its weave; (3) one strip is freshly re-woven in a new colour, its loose threads still hanging — mended behind his back; (4) his cream-coloured braids are tied back with red yarn; (5) a dark bruise from a sling-stone on his bare shoulder. Place: the narrow mouth of the valley between steep cliffs at night: terraces of fitted grey stone above, the torches of the slingers on the heights. Amber light from the cracks in the stony ground below.

jobs.title: Ойка Травница Долины — Забытые, лекарь, Вода (c4-50, Эхо, эпическая)

jobs.subject: Subject: Oika, Herbalist of the Valley, a woman of the valley weavers, a healer of the Water school. Who she is: herbs grow on the valley slopes by kind — below, those against fever, higher, those against pain, at the very top the bitter ones that bring sleep; she knew their weight without scales. At the mouth of the valley, behind the woven shield, there were more wounded than herbs, and she learned to cut a leaf into eight. She counted the wounded on a long thread — one knot for each person she held in her hands. Right now a wounded fighter is carried to her from the shield. Character: tender, quick and unshakable — a small woman with a will like a mountain; her large pale-gold eyes wide and focused, her mouth firm. Pose, the moment of healing: the camera is low; she leans forward toward the right, reaching toward the wounded beyond the right edge. She has exactly two arms: her near hand holds out a bundle of fresh healing herbs, and cool blue light of the Water school flows from the leaves toward the right like clear spring water; her far hand, raised to her chest, holds a long woollen thread crowded with small knots, wound around her wrist and fingers. Details that tell her story: (1) the thread is three cubits long and so dense with knots that there is hardly room for a new one; (2) bundles of herbs hang from her belt in three groups — from the bottom, the middle and the top of the slope; (3) a small bronze knife and a leaf cut into eight pieces in her belt pouch; (4) rolls of striped woven bandages over her shoulder; (5) her cream-coloured braids are tied with green yarn, a few loose from haste. Place: the rocky mouth of the valley at night: a small mountain stream running past her, the dark terraces of fitted stone above, torchlight behind. Blue light rises from the stream below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Hassi the Slinger, a woman of the valley weavers, a swift fighter of the Earth school. Who she is: she wove slings better than cloth. When her river pebbles ran out on the first day, she began to gather the stones of the enemy — hewn and even, as if taken from a wall — and sent them back to those who threw them; people said her stones went home. At night she climbed the mortarless wall the enemy had built, where there is nothing for a finger to hold, onto a ledge above their slingers. Right now she whirls their own stone back at them from the height. Character: fierce, daring and proud; a sharp, feral grin, her pale-gold eyes blazing, her chin lifted. Pose, the moment of the throw: the camera is low; she stands on a narrow ledge high above the valley, turned toward the right, her body twisted into the throw. She has exactly two arms: her near arm whirls a long striped woollen sling in a blurred circle above her head, the pouch swinging out toward the right; her far hand holds another hewn square stone ready at her hip. The stone in the sling glows with amber-orange light of the Earth school and leaves a bright arc in the air. Details that tell her story: (1) the sling is woven of the same striped wool as her tunic; (2) a bag at her hip is full of hewn square stones — the enemy's own; (3) her fingertips are raw and scraped from the climb up the fitted wall; (4) black crow feathers are tied into her cream-coloured braids — as a girl she chased crows from the roofs; (5) behind her rises a wall of huge many-sided grey stones fitted so tightly that no blade would pass between them. Place: a high ledge at dawn above a green valley: terraces of fitted stone, torn rope bridges swinging over a gorge, snowy peaks. Amber light rises from cracks in the ledge below; the wind tugs at her mantle.

jobs.subject: Subject: Rua the Unknotter, a woman of the valley weavers, a battle mage of the Time school. Who she is: the lords of Hatun-Rumi did not write — they tied; on their priests' long cords, in dark double knots of debt, the whole valley was bound. A weaver sees a knot differently from a priest: not what it means but how it is tied. She stole their longest cord and untied the knots of debt with her fingers and her teeth, and each debt went away with the wind — and with it the priests' power. Right now she tears open a cord of debt knots. Character: fierce, relentless and bitterly triumphant; her eyes burning with green light, her teeth bared on the end of the cord. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands turned toward the right, her body taut, her head lowered. She has exactly two arms: her two hands hold a long dark cord stretched between them and rip it apart; the dark double knots along it burst open one after another with flashes of green light, and the empty threads stream away on the wind toward the right, toward the priests beyond the right edge (Time); one end of the cord is caught between her teeth. Details that tell her story: (1) her fingers are crooked and stiff from untying, the knuckles swollen; (2) around her wrist is wound a different thread — a pale woollen one crowded with small knots, which she does not untie; (3) many loose, empty cords whip around her in the wind like snakes; (4) a spindle whorl of fired clay hangs at her neck; (5) a priest's cord-belt, torn, hangs from her own belt. Place: the valley at night under the dark terraces of Hatun-Rumi: a cold wind from the ledges carries empty cords over torn rope bridges. Green light of the Time school bursts from the knots and rises from the grass below.
